summary: We are testing whether expanding the BFS-optimal endgame from 3 to 4 elements reduces worst-case operation count (from 2n-2 to 2n-4) while maintaining the perfect score of 100. This is iteration 3, building on two prior iterations that both achieved score 100 on all 10 test cases (n=1000).
key_points: Single arm (h-main): Replace the k=3 endgame with a k=4 endgame that handles all 23 non-trivial permutations of the last 4 elements via a BFS-derived dispatch table, each resolved in ≤4 operations.
Prediction: Score 100 on all 10 test cases (same as iter-1 and iter-2), with worst-case operations reduced from 1998 to 1996 — a marginal improvement since the score metric clamps at 100.
Confirmation criteria: Score = 100 AND total operations ≤ 1996 on worst case. Refutation: any score < 100 or operations > 1996 would indicate a bug in the 23-case dispatch table.

Risk assessment: This iteration is low-risk optimization at the score ceiling. Both prior iterations already scored 100. The primary value is validating the BFS endgame extension technique and slightly tightening the operation bound.

Skipped arms (ablation, control, dose-response, robustness) are justified: prior iterations already proved the core mechanism essential, score is already at ceiling, and all test cases use n=1000 with no regime variation.
